correctness.rationale: Differentiating the binomial tail telescopes to n·binom(n−1,m−1) z^(m−1)(1−z)^(n−m); the two latent components give opposite derivatives with the same positive factor pq. For 0<h<1, t=h/(1−h) makes the sign that of L(t)=a log(1+t/p)−b log(1+t/q). The numerator of L′ is a−(n−1)p+(a−b)t. With L(0)=0 and growth at infinity of sign a−b, this gives the full strict-sign/one-turn alternatives, also at p=p_c and with either exponent zero. Equal exponents are positive for n≥2 and give the stated comparison with p=1/2; at p=1/2 symmetry gives F=1/2. For n=2,3 the exponents are equal or one is zero, so none can turn. For n=4, m=3, p=4/5 the positive root is t=8/5. Direct integer evaluation of the mixture, using component probabilities 12/13 and 4/13 at the root, gives the claimed endpoint and minimum fractions 512/625, 8704/10985, 4/5. At a positive root the numerator of L′ has already passed its only zero, hence the turning point is nondegenerate. The grid values of the smooth threshold away from ties converge to their hard indicators; the fixed-degree polynomial and two derivatives converge uniformly, preserving a local extremum of the same kind, not necessarily the global phase diagram. value.rationale: The unconditional group adoption fraction is a defined observable in the motivating model, not an arbitrary chosen statistic. Its exact finite-size phase boundary answers when homophily changes from helping to hurting adoption or vice versa, and the minimal four-person witness gives a precise benchmark below both endpoints. These are useful facts about behavioral aggregation without asserting any corresponding epidemic-threshold, prevalence, or policy conclusion.
